2. The plaintiff brought the suit for declaration of his title to and recovery of khas possession in the suit land by evicting the defendants on the basis of his purchase of Touzi No. 314 in revenue sale, and delivery of possession of the same in 1951 after confirmation of the sale, and annulment of encumbrances in Miscellaneous Case No. 151 of 1951. According to the plaintiff he got khas possession in all the lands of the Touzi excepting 'Kha' schedule land which is in possession of the defendant. Hence the suit. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit contending, inter alia, that the suit land does not constitute an under tenure holding but it is an occupancy holding. He claimed that the plaintiff's father settled the disputed land with the defendant and others by 4 pattas on 3.12.1927 and on the same day they made a waqf of the said property by a registered deed of waqf and the defendant was made the Mutwalti. The defendant claimed to have raiyati mokarari right in the land settled with them by the father of the plaintiff. He claimed that since he has acquired a right of occupancy in the suit land he is not liable to be ejected. 

 3. The learned Munsif on consideration of the pattas and other documents produced by the party and subsequent user of the land by the tenants dismissed the suit on the finding that the defendant is an occupancy raiyat. On appeal the Subordinate Judge interpreted the pattas as creating tenure holding in favour of the defendant and decreed the suit. This decision was affirmed by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division.

 4. It appears that land measuring 1.90 acres recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 528 appertaining to Touzi No. 314 is the subject matter of the suit for khas possession. Plaintiff claimed it on the basis of his auction purchase of the Touzi in revenue sale held on 27-9-50 which was confirmed on 27.11.50 and delivery of possession given on 7.4.51. Thereafter all the under tenures appertaining to the said Touzi were annulled in a regular proceeding; and the plaintiff got possession of all lands excepting the suit land. According to the plaintiff he has already possession of .43 acres of land of the said khatian which has been described in schedule "Ka". The suit land has been described in schedule "Kha", to the plaint. C. S. Khatian No. 528 is directly under C.S. KhatianNo. 527 which records the tenure right of the predecessor of the plaintiff. Keramaullah Talukder, father of the plaintiff settled the disputed land with (1) Rabiullah and Yeadullah, (2) Keramatullah, (3) Banari Bibi, and (4) Sonaullah by 4 pattas dated 3.12.27. According to the defendant the pattas created a mokararijote right but according to the Plaintiff it created an under tenure holding. 

 5. Decision of the case depends on interpretation of terms of the pattas. The defendant in support of his case referred to a registered waqfnama dated 3.12.27 by which waqf was created in respect of the land settled by the plaintiff's father Keramatullah Talukder. Sonaullah Talukder was appointed as the Mutwalli. Defendant further showed that the plaintiff's father and after him the plaintiff all along treated the land as mokararijote right and realized rent from the settlement holder. In this connection defendant also referred to a decree in Title Suit No. 171 of 1947 obtained by the plaintiff's father in respect of .43 acres of land purchased by him in a rent sale, and suit was filled for declaration of his title and partition of the same. Plaintiff's father got a decree in that suit. The trial Court in consideration of the evidence led by the parties and referring to the recitals in the pattas arrived at the finding that the defendant was a cultivating raiyatin actual possession of the suit land and so the trial Court held that the defendant acquired occupancy right which was a protected interest. On appeal by the plaintiff the learned Subordinate Judge, however, arrived at a different finding with regard to the nature and character of the interest created by the pattas. Relying on the provisions in the pattas authorizing the settlement holder to engage tenants, and settlement of mokari right at fixed rate, was of the view that the incidents of the settlement indicate beyond any shadow or doubt that it was a tenure and not an occupancy right granted to the defendant by the pattas. According to him the original purpose being use of land by engaging tenants, tenant's mere user of the same as a cultivating raiyat, cannot change the nature and character of the holding, the learned Subordinate Judge arrived at the finding that inception of the tenancies shows in clear terms that the defendant took settlement of the tenure and not of raiyati right, and as such be cannot acquire occupancy right in the tenure by cultivating the land for a long time nor he can acquire any occupancy right by virtue of his being a settled raiyat in that village. The learned Subordinate Judge concluded with the finding that the defendant is not an occupancy raiyat but a tenure holder, so his interest is not protected under section 37 of the Revenue Sale Law. This decision was affirmed by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in second appeal. 

 6. Mr. B. B. Roy Chowdhury, the learned Advocate, appearing for the appellant submitted that the learned Subordinate Judge as well as the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division failed to properly appreciate section 5 of the Bengal Tenancy Act, which has defined "tenure holder" and consequently failed to appreciate the pattas Exhibit D series in the light of the said definition, and this led to an erroneous, decision that the pattas created a tenure holding and not a raiyati holding Mr. Roy Chowdhury further submitted that the dakhilas Exhibit A series, the decree passed in Title Suit No. 171 of 1947, Exhibit E series clearly show that the landlord treated the right of the defendant in the disputed property as a raiyati tenancy. 

 7. The tenure-holder as defined in section S of the Bengal Tenancy Act means primarily a person who has acquired from a proprietor or from another tenure-holder a right to hold land for the purpose of collecting rents or for bringing it under cultivation by establishing tenants on it, and includes also the successors-in-interest of persons who have acquired such a right. The definition of raiyat as it was before the amendment of 1928 was that-means primarily a person who has acquired a right to hold land for the purpose of cultivating it by himself or by members of his family or by hired servants or with the aid of partners and includes also the successor in interest of persons who had acquired such a right. The definition was slightly modified by the amendment of 1928. After amendment "Raiyat" means primarily a person who acquired a right to hold land for the purpose of cultivating it by himself or by members of his family or by servants or labourers or with the aid of partners and also includes successors in interest of persons who have acquired such a right. Sub-section (1) of section 5 deanes "Tenure holder". A tenure-holder means primarily a person who has acquired from a proprietor or from another tenure holder a right to hold land for the purpose of collecting rents or bringing it under cultivation by establishing tenants on it and includes also the successors in interest of persons who have acquired such a right. The pattas in question being prior to the amendment of the Bengal Tenancy Act by Act IV of 1928, the old sub-section (2) of section 5 should be referred to for the definition, "Raiyat" means primarily a person who has acquired a right to hold land for the purpose of cultivating it by himself or by members of his family or by hired servants, or with the aid of partners, and includes also the successors in interest of persons who have acquired such a right Sub, section (4) of section 5 provide the guidance to find out whether a tenant is a tenure-bolder or a raiyat.  11. The above noted recitals show that the lessee was allowed to hold the land at fixed rate of rent; and it authorized the lessee to collect rent by setting up tenants on the land. The pattas land was recorded in C S. Khatian No. 528 as “মধ্যস্বত্ব চিরস্থায়ী স্বত্বের”…… With reference to the terms in the pattas the lower Appellate Court held that defendant is a tenure bolder. According to him, since the inception of the tenancy shows in clear terms that the defendant took settlement of the land with the right of a tenure-holder and not with a raiyati right. Thus it appears that the learned Subordinate Judge confined his consideration on the question of nature of the tenancy merely with reference to recitals of the patta but without any consideration as to the nature of use of the land by the lessee since its inception. The plaintiff in this suit prayed for khas possession of 1 90 acres of land recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 528 on the basic of his auction purchase in revenue sale of Touzi No. 314 of Bogra Collectorate. According to the plaintiff’s case, he has already got possession of.43 acres or land of the same khatian, but due to obstruction he did not succeed in taking possession of 1.90 acres of land of the said khatian. Defendant No.1 gave a total denial about the annulment of the encumbrance and their knowledge about the said proceeding with regard to .43 acres in the possession of the plaintiff. His case is that the plaintiff's father Keramatullah Talukder took khas possession of it as putnidar in Title Suit No. 171 of 1947 of the Munsif, First Court, Bogra. According to the defendant, plaintiff never took possession of it. The defendant's further case is that plaintiff's father settled the disputed land with (1) Rabiullah and Yadullah; (2) Karamatullah Talukder, (3) Banari Bibi, and (4) Sonaullah by 4 pattas dated 3-12-1927 in makarrarijote right, and on the same day they made a wakf by a registered deed of wakf and the defendant became the mutwalli. The mere fact that a person has acquired from a proprietor or from another tenure-holder a right to hold land for the purpose of collecting rent is not sufficient to prove that he is a tenure-holder. It must be proved on evidence that since the inception of the tenancy land was let out for agricultural or horticultural purpose. This principle, as it appears from the judgment of the lower Appellate Court and that of the High Court Division, was not followed in determining the controversy between the parties on the question of nature of the tenancy created by the pattas Exhibit D series dated 3.12.1927. 

 12. The defendant's specific case is that by the patta a raiyati with occupancy right was created and not a tenure as claimed by the plaintiff, and this gets support from the use of the land by the defendant from the very inception of the tenancy. The defendant led the evidence to prove that the land has been under direct cultivation of the defendant. Defendant filed certain dakhilas Exhibit. A to A(5) of which Exhibit A is in the hand-writing of the plaintiff and Exhibits A to A( 5) are in the hand writing of Keramatullah Mondal, plaintiff's father. C.S. Khatian No. 528 is included in all these dakhilas except A(2) and A(3). With reference to these dakhilas the learned Munsif rightly observed that it no longer lies in the mouth of the plaintiff to say that defendants are "Niskar tenure-holder as recorded in khatian and not raiyati." The defendant also filed a decree made in Title Suit No. 171 of 1947 (Exhibit E) which shows that the suit was brought by Keramatullah Mondal on the basis or auction purchase of schedule "Ka" land in rent sale. The decree also belies the statement of the plaintiff that he got possession of schedule 'Ka' land on the basis of revenue sale and got possession through the Collectorate. With reference to the above mentioned materials the learned Munsif correctly arrived at the finding that by the pattas raiyati with occupancy right was created, and the suit land does not appertain to an under-tenure holding as claimed by the plaintiff. By the pattas dated 3-12-1927 a tenancy in the nature of makarrari jote right was created and the interest thus acquired by the defendant is protected from annulment under section 37 of the Revenue sale law. In this context it may be mentioned that the recitals in the pattas lend considerable support to the defendant's case that “স্বাধীন প্রজালিলি” was not the dominant purpose of creation of the tenancy by the pattas Exhibit D series. It mentions that the pattas created an occupancy raiyati interest with fixed jama. It recites, inter alia- 

 The pattas also authorize the tenant to enjoy the tenancy with the rights amongst others- “পঙ্করিনী খনন ও ভরন ইষ্টক রিম্মিত পোন্ডশ দালান কি মসজিদ আদি কি বক্ষাদি রোপন ও ছেদন করনের ক্ষমতাযক্তে পরম সাথে পত্র পৌত্রাদি ওয়ারীশানগণ ক্রমে চিরকাল ভোগ দখল ও তছরুপ করিতে থাকহঃ” 

 The tenancy was created in 1927 and the suit was filed in 1959,"and during this long period of 32 years the Ian has although been used by the tenant for cultivation by himself and for other purposes In view of the rights conferred upon the tenant by the pattas and the admitted fact that the defendant never set up any tenant on the land and he used the land for himself by cultivation and for other purposes. I am of the opinion that by the pattas Exhibit D series mokarrari jote with fixed rent with occupancy right was created in favour of the patta holders, including the defendant; and such tenancy is protected from annulment. The learned Subordinate Judge on misconception of law and facts erroneously reversed the judgment of the trial Court and learned Judge of the High Court Division affirmed the same.
